full.description: This is a photomicrograph of splenic tissue showing characteristic pathological changes. The section displays prominent periarterial fibrosis, often referred to as "onion skinning," surrounding a central arteriole. There is also a notable infiltration of lymphocytes and inflammatory cells within the splenic pulp. These histological findings are classic for systemic lupus erythematosus involving the spleen.

blind.description: This is a microscopic image of splenic tissue. It displays prominent periarterial fibrosis and an accumulation of atypical immunoblastic cells near the splenic arteriole. These findings are characteristic of an immunoblastic reaction often seen in viral infections such as influenza, or associated with conditions like lupus erythematosus.

random.description: This is a microscopic histological image showing a section of tissue, likely skin or soft tissue, stained with H&E. The field displays a dense inflammatory infiltrate composed predominantly of lymphocytes and plasma cells surrounding blood vessels. There is also evidence of fibrosis and collagen deposition within the stroma. These histological features are characteristic of a chronic inflammatory process, potentially related to a localized vasculitis or a specific dermatological condition.
